findings.description: The start-up sequence treats a code 8 report as a detection, but permits status-high and task release only when no fault has been detected since reset. SWR-LAT-010 and SWR-LAT-011 require code 8 to leave start-up continuing unless the latch is set.
findings.requested_change: Distinguish a code 8 report from a fault that prevents normal start-up, including in the status-high and task-release conditions.

findings.description: The fault manager says every detection commands outputs low and inhibits both watchdogs, yet it also receives code 8. SWR-LAT-010 requires code 8 not to enter the safe state by itself, and CON-SUP-137 requires watchdog servicing to continue.
findings.requested_change: Specify a separate code 8 handling path that records and reports it without commanding the safe state or inhibiting watchdog service, except for the latch reaction at the third detection.

findings.description: The manager records history and increments the fault count on detection. SWR-SVC-007, SWR-SVC-009 and SWR-SVC-010 define these in terms of reports made; SWR-DIA-001 permits a fault interrupted by a watchdog reset to have no report.
findings.requested_change: Define when a report is made and update the retained report count and history consistently with that event, including interrupted fault handling.

findings.description: Compare events are armed exactly at the limit, but a measured value equal to the limit is within it. The item does not specify a later comparison if the task remains unstarted or executing, so a single event at equality can miss the violation required by SWR-TIM-001 and SWR-TIM-002.
findings.requested_change: Specify how the supervisor detects a continuing violation after equality within the 100 µs deadline, including event ordering at the limit.

findings.description: The scheduler releases the three 10 ms tasks and T_DIAG in a fixed pattern, although SWR-CFG-007 requires the task set, periods and release order to come from configuration so they can change without changing supervisor code.
findings.requested_change: Define scheduling in terms of the validated configuration, with the stated four-task schedule as the default rather than a fixed algorithm.

findings.description: The highest-priority task below the timer handler releases application tasks and then performs the end-of-cycle checkpoint check in the same sequence. It specifies no wait or scheduling point that lets those tasks execute and report checkpoints before the check.
findings.requested_change: Specify the execution contexts and ordering that allow the released tasks to run and submit their checkpoints before the end-of-cycle check, including the 100 ms task.

findings.description: The start-up task runs alone before other tasks start, yet SWC-SUP-011 transmits the RST and code 8 messages in the diagnostic task. SWR-RST-002 and SWR-RST-003 require those transmissions within 10 ms of reset classification, including while start-up checks are running.
findings.requested_change: Define how diagnostic transmission executes during start-up and meets both message deadlines and their required order.

findings.description: The status-high request checks fault state and then writes the pin, while the interrupt-context fault manager can command the pins low. Atomic individual pin writes do not prevent an interrupt between the check and the high write, which can leave the status high after a fault.
findings.requested_change: Specify synchronization or an equivalent ordering mechanism that prevents a status-high write after fault detection or latch setting.

findings.description: The inhibit flag can be set from interrupt context while a task services a watchdog. Atomic access to the flag alone does not prevent a fault interrupt between checking the flag and issuing a refresh, contrary to SWR-WDG-001.
findings.requested_change: Define synchronization or hardware-supported ordering that prevents a watchdog service after fault detection, including an interrupt during a service call.

findings.description: Invalid retained content is treated as power-on state. On a software or watchdog reset this can clear the latch, detection counts and history, conflicting with SWR-LAT-007, SWR-LAT-013 and SWR-LAT-014.
findings.requested_change: Distinguish confirmed power-on reset from invalid retained content after other resets, and specify a reaction that preserves the required retention behavior.

findings.description: On a full report queue the interface says the new report is queued after a bounded retry, but gives no storage for it while the queue remains full. The capacity covers only one cycle of reports, while SWR-DIA-001 requires each applicable report within 10 ms.
findings.requested_change: Define bounded admission, pending storage and transmission behavior for simultaneous or successive reports, and show how the required deadlines are met.

findings.description: The item states that each pin write is atomic and that pins are inputs from any reset, but cites software requirements and no controlled hardware reference supporting those hardware properties. CON-SUP-002 identifies RM0486 without a section or page.
findings.requested_change: Cite the controlled hardware reference for the claimed access and reset properties, or record the unsupported properties as open points.

findings.description: SWR-TIM-001 and SWR-TIM-002 require detection no later than 100 µs after the limit expires. The element schedules decisive event B at limit + 100 µs, then allows a further 100 µs of handler latency, permitting detection 200 µs after expiry.
findings.requested_change: Specify a detection mechanism and latency bound that meet the 100 µs deadline while preserving the equality rule.

findings.description: The element says a start or completion event cancels pending compare events and event B raises nothing if the task has since started or completed. A start or completion after the configured limit but before event B is processed can therefore escape detection, despite SWR-TIM-001 through SWR-TIM-004.
findings.requested_change: Define how the stored event instants are compared with the limits and how a late start or completion is reported even if it occurs before the compare handler runs.

findings.description: The description says a detection count returns to zero only after 60 seconds of fault-free operation and never at power-on, but later says power-on clears the counts. SWR-LAT-009 requires the counts to be cleared at power-on.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the contradictory power-on behavior and specify clearing the detection counts as required by SWR-LAT-009.

findings.description: SWR-DIA-001 requires each applicable fault report within 10 ms. This interface explicitly allows later reports in a larger burst to miss that deadline; OP-SWC-009 defers the burst limit to verification, which cannot establish the missing architecture-level guarantee.
findings.requested_change: Provide a supported transmission and admission design that meets the deadline for all required reports, or raise a blocking decision on the conflicting burst and timing requirements.

findings.description: The cycle-end compare is required to occur within each 10 ms cycle after the execution-limit expiry of every released task, including T_DIAG. CON-SUP-103 gives T_DIAG a 20 ms execution limit, so its expiry cannot precede the end of its release cycle.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the cycle-end scheduling and supervision interaction against the configured T_DIAG limit and the end-of-cycle flow-check requirement.

findings.description: The start-up task cites OP-SWC-001 for execution time but states no task stack or other memory budget, and that open point addresses execution budgets rather than memory.
findings.requested_change: Allocate a justified memory budget to the start-up task or record the missing budget as an open point.

findings.description: The control-cycle task cites OP-SWC-001 for execution time but states no task stack or other memory budget, and that open point addresses execution budgets rather than memory.
findings.requested_change: Allocate a justified memory budget to the control-cycle task or record the missing budget as an open point.

findings.description: The component states that it detects an alive fault after two consecutive periods without a completed execution, but identifies no periodic invocation or timer event that evaluates the alive counter. Its described compare events cover start and execution limits only.
findings.requested_change: Specify when and in which context alive supervision is evaluated, including how elapsed periods and completions produce the code 1 notification.

findings.description: The code 8 path sets the latch at the third detection and explicitly updates the latch at detection, before report completion. SWR-LAT-004 requires the latch when the code 8 report is made at start-up; the architecture defines a report as made only on the completion notification. These events can differ, including when reset interrupts transmission.
findings.requested_change: Align the code 8 latch transition with SWR-LAT-004 and define its handling when the report does not complete.

findings.description: The stated start-up order begins with reset-cause classification, although SWR-SAF-003 requires configuring the control outputs and status signal low before any other start-up step. The task also enters idle when any fault was detected, although SWR-LAT-011 requires start-up to continue after a code 8 report.
findings.requested_change: Specify output configuration as the first start-up action and distinguish the code 8 continuation path from faults that prevent normal start-up.

findings.description: SWR-TIM-001 and SWR-TIM-002 require detection no later than 100 µs after the configured limit expires. The component arms its compare at the limit plus one 100 µs unit, then permits a further 100 µs entry-plus-decision latency. That permits detection 200 µs after the configured limit.
findings.requested_change: Define the compare and decision timing so the worst-case detection time satisfies the 100 µs bound while preserving the equality rule.

findings.description: SWR-LAT-012 counts a code 8 report when it is made, and SWR-LAT-004 latches on the third counted detection. The component increments the code 8 count even when transmission is interrupted and no report is made; a later completed report can therefore latch after fewer than three reports have been made.
findings.requested_change: Align code 8 counting and latch behavior for interrupted reports with SWR-LAT-004 and SWR-LAT-012.

findings.description: The task queues the code 8 report and services transmission between CRC chunks, but does not require report completion before checking the latch and permitting normal start-up. If checks finish before transmission completes, supervised tasks could be released before the third code 8 report sets the latch.
findings.requested_change: Specify the completion ordering and bounded error path needed to ensure the code 8 latch decision is made before permitting supervised task release.

findings.description: SWR-DIA-001 requires each applicable fault report within 10 ms. The interface permits later reports in a burst to miss that deadline, and OP-SWC-009 defers the burst limit to verification without establishing the required guarantee.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the report deadline for every permitted fault burst at architecture or requirements level; do not defer the missing guarantee to verification.

findings.description: SWR-TIM-001 and SWR-TIM-002 require detection no later than 100 µs after the configured limit expires. The compare is armed at the limit plus 100 µs, with another 100 µs allowed for entry and decision, permitting detection 200 µs after the configured limit.
findings.requested_change: Specify a detection mechanism and latency bound that satisfy both the deadline and the equality rules.

findings.description: SWR-LAT-012 counts a code 8 report when it is made, and SWR-LAT-004 latches on the third counted detection. The component increments the retained code 8 count even when transmission is interrupted and no report is made; a later completed report can therefore latch after fewer than three reports.
findings.requested_change: Update the code 8 count and latch at the report event consistently with SWR-LAT-004 and SWR-LAT-012, including interrupted transmissions.

findings.description: The start-up task queues the code 8 report and services transmission between CRC chunks, but does not require report completion before checking the latch and permitting normal start-up. Checks could finish before the third code 8 report completes and sets the latch.
findings.requested_change: Specify the sequencing that prevents task release and status-high while the pending code 8 report could set the latch.

findings.description: SWR-RES-001 limits normal-operation supervisor execution to 10% over any 1 s window. OP-SWC-001 defers task and interrupt execution budgets and the core clock, so the stated 500 µs CRC allowance plus the other execution contexts cannot be shown to fit that limit or the diagnostic and detection deadlines.
findings.requested_change: Allocate and justify compatible execution budgets and scheduling bounds at architecture level, or record the missing architecture-level decisions as blocking open points.

findings.description: The tenth-cycle flow check can find T_DIAG missing even while it is within its configured 20 ms execution limit. OP-SWC-011 identifies the unresolved interaction with the 10 ms cycle and asks whether the checkpoint is judged in the release cycle or later.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the flow-check and T_DIAG timing interaction against the controlling requirements and specify the resulting sequence.

findings.description: SWR-DIA-001 requires each applicable fault report within 10 ms. SWC-SUP-039 calculates that four simultaneous reports behind an answer line can take up to 12.9 ms. OP-SWC-013 records the unresolved requirement-level decision.
findings.requested_change: Resolve the interaction between report deadlines and an answer already in progress, then specify an architecture that satisfies the resulting requirement.

findings.description: The flow check is performed at the end of the 10 ms cycle, but T_DIAG has a 20 ms execution limit and may not yet have supplied its checkpoint. OP-SWC-011 identifies the unresolved interpretation of SWR-FLW-001.
findings.requested_change: Resolve when T_DIAG's checkpoint must be evaluated and make the flow-check sequence consistent with that decision.

findings.description: The diagnostic task runs below the application tasks, yet SWC-SUP-039 assumes it runs within 1 ms of a report submission. SWC-SUP-061 supplies no application execution or scheduling bound that guarantees this response; T_DIAG alone has a 20 ms execution limit.
findings.requested_change: Specify and justify scheduling and response-time bounds that let diagnostic transmission meet the applicable report and service deadlines under the permitted application workload.

findings.description: DEC-SWC-013 now allocates 920 µs per 10 ms cycle, but the budgets are unverified targets and OP-SWC-012 leaves the core clock and CRC throughput to detailed design. The architecture does not establish that the 500 µs CRC segment and remaining work can be achieved on the configured platform.
findings.requested_change: Provide an architecture-level basis for the execution allocations and their feasibility at the configured core clock, or identify the unresolved platform decision as a blocking open point.

findings.description: The scheduler represents configured periods as whole 10 ms tick counts, but SWC-SUP-001 validates only zero periods, unknown tasks and limits longer than periods. OP-SWC-005 leaves non-integral periods and their validation unresolved, so accepted configuration data need not have the timing it specifies.
findings.requested_change: Define and validate the supported period range and tick granularity, or obtain the necessary configuration decision before accepting such data.

findings.description: The flow check occurs at the end of the 10 ms cycle, while T_DIAG can have a 20 ms execution limit. A task still within its execution limit may therefore have no checkpoint at the check.
findings.requested_change: Resolve how T_DIAG is evaluated and specify a consistent flow-check sequence.

findings.description: DEC-SWC-015 raises diagnostic priority, but the claimed 1 ms response assumes only one timer-handler entry. SWC-SUP-062 allows start and execution compare events for multiple released tasks; coincident events and their interference are not bounded by the response analysis.
findings.requested_change: Analyze the maximum coincident interrupt workload and demonstrate the diagnostic response and service-answer deadlines for that workload.

findings.description: DEC-SWC-016 derives a conditional minimum clock using a target of 10 cycles per byte, but neither that CRC throughput nor the remaining 420 µs of per-cycle work is established. OP-SWC-012 leaves the configured clock and feasibility confirmation to design.
findings.requested_change: Provide a supported feasibility basis for the CRC and other execution allocations at an identified configuration, or resolve the required platform decision before relying on the budgets.

findings.description: The 60 µs detection bound assumes at most one 50 µs handler latency. Multiple tasks can have the same release and start limit, so their compare events may coincide; the architecture does not bound the time to decide every pending limit.
findings.requested_change: Specify handling of simultaneous compare events and demonstrate that every applicable detection meets its 100 µs bound.
